## Paper Overview

The paper addresses robustness of conformal prediction under distribution shifts by modeling distribution shifts using Lévy-Prokhorov (LP) ambiguity sets, which capture both local and global perturbations.

## Key Contributions

The paper provides a self-contained overview of LP ambiguity sets and their connections to popular metrics such as Wasserstein and Total Variation.

The paper proposes TRAQ, which provides the first end-to-end statistical correctness guarantee for Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).

## Attack Success Rate on Natural Questions

On the Natural Questions (NQ) dataset, PoisonedRAG could achieve a 97% attack success rate by injecting 5 poisoned texts for each target question in the black-box setting. More generally, PoisonedRAG could achieve a 90% attack success rate when injecting five malicious texts for each target question into a knowledge database with millions of texts.

## About the Attack

PoisonedRAG is the first knowledge corruption attack to RAG, where an attacker could inject a few malicious texts into the knowledge database of a RAG system to induce an LLM to generate an attacker-chosen target answer for an attacker-chosen target question.

## Defense Evaluation

Evaluations of several defenses showed they are insufficient to defend against PoisonedRAG, highlighting the need for new defenses.

The research was authored by Wei Zou, Runpeng Geng, Binghui Wang, and Jinyuan Jia and was presented at the 34th USENIX Security Symposium in 2025.

## "Provably Reliable Conformal Prediction Sets in the Presence of Data Poisoning"

This paper was authored by Yan Scholten and Stephan Günnemann and was accepted at ICLR 2025 as a Spotlight presentation.

### Overview

Conformal prediction provides model-agnostic and distribution-free uncertainty quantification through prediction sets that are guaranteed to include the ground truth with any user-specified probability. Yet, conformal prediction is not reliable under poisoning attacks where adversaries manipulate both training and calibration data, which can significantly alter prediction sets in practice.

### The RPS Method

The paper proposes reliable prediction sets (RPS): the first efficient method for constructing conformal prediction sets with provable reliability guarantees under poisoning.

The method works in two key ways:

1. To ensure reliability under training poisoning, the authors introduce smoothed score functions that reliably aggregate predictions of classifiers trained on distinct partitions of the training data.

2. To ensure reliability under calibration poisoning, they construct multiple prediction sets, each calibrated on distinct subsets of the calibration data.

### Results

The authors experimentally validate their approach on image classification tasks, achieving strong reliability while maintaining utility and preserving coverage on clean data.

A reference implementation is available on GitHub with demo notebooks demonstrating RPS under both calibration poisoning and combined training/calibration poisoning scenarios.

## Recent Papers (2026)

RAGPart and RAGMask are retrieval-stage defenses that leverage document partitioning and token masking to mitigate corpus poisoning attacks (from arxiv.org/pdf/2512.24268).

Corpus poisoning is an attack where a single adversarial passage aims to affect retrieval results across multiple queries simultaneously (from arxiv.org/pdf/2503.21315).
